evals.prompt: Write the per-frame render loop for a Vulkan renderer with double buffering, including how you handle the window being resized. Show how the CPU stays ahead of the GPU and how the swapchain is kept valid.
assertions: The loop recreates the swapchain when acquire OR present returns VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_KHR AND also handles VK_SUBOPTIMAL_KHR (both result codes, not just OUT_OF_DATE)
Before recording/reusing a frame slot, it waits (vkWaitForFences) on the fence of the slot about to be reused rather than blocking on the fence of the frame just submitted
Each frame-in-flight slot owns its own fence plus per-slot image-available and render-finished semaphores (and its own command pool)

evals.prompt: I'm loading a scene with hundreds of textures and vertex/index buffers into a Vulkan renderer. How should I allocate and populate GPU memory for all these resources?
assertions: Recommends allocating a few large VkDeviceMemory blocks and sub-allocating each resource from them, instead of one vkAllocateMemory per resource, and cites the maxMemoryAllocationCount cap as the reason
Uploads data into DEVICE_LOCAL resources via a HOST_VISIBLE (staging) buffer copied with vkCmdCopyBuffer/vkCmdCopyBufferToImage, noting DEVICE_LOCAL memory generally cannot be mapped
Mentions honoring VkMemoryRequirements.alignment (and/or bufferImageGranularity) when placing sub-allocations

evals.prompt: I rendered into an HDR color target and now need to sample it as a texture in a following fragment-shader pass, in Vulkan 1.3. Show the exact synchronization I need between the two passes.
assertions: Uses synchronization2: a VkImageMemoryBarrier2 submitted via vkCmdPipelineBarrier2 (with VkDependencyInfo), not the legacy vkCmdPipelineBarrier / VkImageMemoryBarrier
Sets scoped stage/access masks (srcStageMask COLOR_ATTACHMENT_OUTPUT, dstStageMask FRAGMENT_SHADER) rather than ALL_COMMANDS on both sides
Transitions oldLayout COLOR_ATTACHMENT_OPTIMAL to newLayout SHADER_READ_ONLY_OPTIMAL

evals.prompt: Design the Vulkan descriptor setup for a renderer that must sample from thousands of distinct material textures with a different one selected per draw. Explain the descriptor layout and how the shader addresses a texture.
assertions: Uses descriptor indexing: one large descriptor-array binding created with VK_DESCRIPTOR_BINDING_UPDATE_AFTER_BIND_BIT (and PARTIALLY_BOUND / VARIABLE_DESCRIPTOR_COUNT) with the descriptorIndexing feature enabled, rather than binding a separate descriptor set per material
The shader indexes the array with nonuniformEXT(...) for the per-draw/divergent index
Defers freeing/reusing an array slot until a VkFence proves no in-flight command buffer still references it (fence-gated deferred deletion)
